hunks.baseline: The moment Jin Taekyung’s voice reached the Doppelganger’s ears, two questions surfaced in its mind, frozen like a statue.
hunks.sol: The moment Jin Taekyung’s voice reached its ears, the Doppelganger froze like a statue. Two questions sprang to mind.

hunks.baseline: Magic manifested solely according to the caster’s will.
hunks.sol: Magic manifested according to the caster’s will alone.

hunks.baseline: And, naturally, the Doppelganger had used Blink only on itself.
hunks.sol: And the Doppelganger had, of course, cast Blink on itself alone.

hunks.baseline: Even a full-blown psychopath with a mind that had spun around thirty-five times wouldn’t do something insane like cast a dangerous movement spell alongside Jin Taekyung—a man who could break the Doppelganger’s neck thirty-six times in the blink of an eye.
hunks.sol: Even a full-blown psychopath whose mind had spun around thirty-five times wouldn’t be crazy enough to cast a dangerous movement spell on Jin Taekyung too. The man could break its neck thirty-six times in the blink of an eye.

hunks.baseline: In the end, there was only one answer.
hunks.sol: There was only one answer.

hunks.baseline: *Regardless of my will… he interfered with the Blink spell.*
hunks.sol: *He interfered with my Blink spell… against my will.*

hunks.baseline: A theory completed after years of research by the scholarly Grand Mage named Siegfried Bassman surfaced among the memories it had absorbed.
hunks.sol: A theory the scholarly Grand Mage Siegfried Bassman had developed after years of research surfaced among the memories the Doppelganger had absorbed.

hunks.baseline: The Doppelganger felt a chill sweep through its entire body. As it watched Jin Taekyung stagger to his feet, a second unanswered question lingered in its eyes.
hunks.sol: A chill swept through its body. As it watched Jin Taekyung stagger to his feet, the second question remained.

hunks.baseline: It could accept the mana interference. The man was a monster, after all.
hunks.sol: It could set the mana interference aside. The man was a monster, after all.

hunks.baseline: It was absurd—utterly absurd—but perhaps this close-combat Hunter really did have mana control that surpassed even a Grand Mage’s.
hunks.sol: Absurd as it was—utterly absurd—perhaps a close-combat Hunter really did possess mana control surpassing even a Grand Mage’s.

hunks.baseline: But the Blink spell just now had been an utterly irrational and dangerous attempt.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: The Doppelganger had nearly been torn apart for breaking the taboo, and it had to sacrifice dozens of lives to heal its body. There was no point saying more.
hunks.sol: But that Blink had been an outrageously dangerous attempt. The Doppelganger itself had nearly been torn apart for breaking the taboo and had sacrificed dozens of lives to heal. What more was there to say?

hunks.baseline: Hearing Jin Taekyung mumble, the Doppelganger’s mind went hazy for a moment.
hunks.sol: The Doppelganger nearly lost its senses at Jin Taekyung’s mutter.

hunks.baseline: That made no sense.
It felt betrayed. Even if Jin Taekyung were an ogre, shouldn’t he at least have lost an arm or a leg or two, out of basic decency?
hunks.sol: It made no sense. Even if Jin Taekyung were an ogre, surely basic decency demanded that he lose an arm or a leg. Maybe two.

hunks.baseline: The Doppelganger had no idea that Jin Taekyung’s physique—once called the Heavenly Martial Physique in Murim—had long since surpassed its limits, enough to withstand even a Blink spell that broke the taboo.
hunks.sol: The Doppelganger had no idea that Jin Taekyung’s muscles and bones—called the Heavenly Martial Physique back in Murim—had long since surpassed the limits of what even that taboo-breaking Blink could shatter.

hunks.baseline: Still, even without knowing the circumstances, the Doppelganger could easily grasp one truth.
hunks.sol: But it could grasp one truth without knowing why.

hunks.baseline: The thoughts brought on by that immense shock were long and complicated, but the time swept away by it lasted no more than an instant.
Just a few seconds.
hunks.sol: The shock set off a long, tangled train of thought. In reality, only a few seconds passed.

hunks.baseline: And at the end of the suffocating silence pressing down on everything came the Doppelganger’s shout, ringing out like a scream.
hunks.sol: Then the Doppelganger’s cry tore through the suffocating silence.

hunks.baseline: The silence shattered.

At the same time, the world that had momentarily stopped began moving again. The fanatics, who had been staring blankly back and forth between Jin Taekyung and their great Prophet in that slowed-down moment, sprang into action.
hunks.sol: The silence shattered. The fanatics, who had stood staring between Jin Taekyung and their great Prophet as though time had slowed, sprang into action.

hunks.baseline: Shouts and the sharp whistle of incoming attacks rang out from every direction.
Looking at the countless flashes hurtling toward him, Jin Taekyung suddenly opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: Shouts and the whistle of attacks came from every direction. Countless flashes streaked toward Jin Taekyung, and he opened his mouth.

hunks.baseline: His vomit scattered before a drop of blood could.
hunks.sol: Vomit sprayed into the air before a drop of blood did.

hunks.baseline: The price of hitching a ride on the Blink spell was a hellish bout of motion sickness.
hunks.sol: The price of hitching a ride on Blink was a hellish bout of motion sickness.

hunks.baseline: I tried to hold it in. I thought I could.
hunks.sol: I’d tried to hold it in. I’d thought I could.

hunks.baseline: Goddammit. I’d been about to say something cool.
hunks.sol: Fuck. I’d been about to say something cool.

hunks.baseline: Instead, vomit came pouring out of my mouth, splattering in a rush. Bent over like a grub, I hurriedly rolled across the ground.
hunks.sol: Vomit came pouring out instead. Bent over like a grub, I hurriedly rolled across the ground.

hunks.baseline: A chill. I felt a sharp blade cut off a whole handful of my hair.
As the auras flying in from all sides grazed my body, stinging pain flared across my skin.
hunks.sol: A chill ran over my scalp. A sharp blade had cut off a whole handful of my hair. Aura-laden weapons flew in from all sides, grazing my body and leaving stinging pain in their wake.

hunks.baseline: *After coming all this way, I have to roll around like a lazy donkey?*
hunks.sol: *After coming all this way, I’m rolling around like a lazy donkey?*

hunks.baseline: Tears blurred my vision. The one small mercy was that those fanatics hadn’t expected this either.
hunks.sol: Tears blurred my vision. The one small mercy was that the fanatics hadn’t expected this either.

hunks.baseline: What kind of lunatic lands in the middle of a crowd of enemies and starts vomiting? I forced my churning stomach to settle and swung the thing in my hand.
hunks.sol: What kind of lunatic lands in the middle of his enemies and starts vomiting? I fought down the churn in my stomach and swung the thing in my hand.

hunks.baseline: The Prophet’s arm, torn off in the aftermath of the Blink spell, made an excellent club.
hunks.sol: The Prophet’s arm, torn off during Blink, made an excellent club.

hunks.baseline: The three fanatics nearest me fell like dominoes.
hunks.sol: The three nearest fanatics fell like dominoes.

hunks.baseline: I hurled the ruined arm like an axe, then stamped down with a stomp in the middle of the enemies packed tightly around me.
hunks.sol: I hurled the ruined arm like an axe, then stamped my foot in the middle of the enemies packed around me.

hunks.baseline: A shock wave packed with a tremendous rumble plunged the ground several meters around me.
The fanatics lost their footing and staggered. Their weapons, thrown off course along with their owners, whistled past my body.
hunks.sol: A shock wave rumbled outward. The ground sank for several meters in every direction, and the fanatics staggered as they lost their footing. Their weapons veered off course with them and swept past my body.

hunks.baseline: I felt the aura and wind pressure carried by the blades graze my skin, leaving tiny cuts.
hunks.sol: The aura and wind pressure carried by the blades left fine cuts in my skin.

hunks.baseline: That alone told me they were skilled fighters.
hunks.sol: That alone told me how skilled they were.

hunks.baseline: I’d counted hundreds of them.

The followers the Doppelganger had raised somewhere in a desolate desert no one could find were every bit as capable as the elite forces of the World Hunter Federation, fighting a fierce battle just a hundred meters away.
hunks.sol: And I’d counted hundreds of them. The followers the Doppelganger had raised somewhere in a desolate desert no one could find were a match for the World Hunter Federation’s elite, locked in battle barely a hundred meters away.

hunks.baseline: The Doppelganger and these disgusting followers of its were all shit from the same cesspit.
hunks.sol: The Doppelganger and its disgusting followers were all shit from the same cesspit.

hunks.baseline: I swallowed the curses rising in me and stretched out both hands.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the curses rising in my throat and thrust out both hands.

hunks.baseline: The fanatics who looked like tanks raised round, enchanted shields to block the way. But they were too late to stop the ten Finger Qi attacks I fired.
hunks.sol: Fanatics who looked like tanks raised round, enchanted shields across my path. They weren’t enough to stop the ten streaks of Finger Qi I’d fired a step ahead of them.

hunks.baseline: A gust of wind swept through, and ten fanatics fell like reed leaves.
hunks.sol: The wind blew, and ten fanatics fell like reed leaves.

hunks.baseline: Through the opening that appeared for an instant, I caught a glimpse of the back of someone who had disappeared from view.
hunks.sol: Through the gap that opened for an instant, I caught a glimpse of someone’s back. I’d lost sight of him for a moment.

hunks.baseline: It was only for the briefest moment, but I saw it clearly and put the pieces together.
The bastard was leaving the battlefield.
hunks.sol: The glimpse was brief, but I’d seen enough. The bastard was leaving the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: Using the countless followers it had raised as bait. Stepping across their blood like a carpet as it fled somewhere beyond my reach.
hunks.sol: He was using the countless followers he’d raised as bait, treading across their blood like a carpet as he fled beyond my reach.

hunks.baseline: Just as it always had. And…
hunks.sol: Just as he always had. And…

hunks.baseline: *It’ll keep doing the same thing from now on.*
hunks.sol: *He’ll keep doing it.*

hunks.baseline: I still didn’t know what plan the bastard had spent more than thirty years building, but I had to bring it down with my own hands here today.
hunks.sol: I still didn’t know what plan the bastard had spent more than thirty years building. But I had to bring it down here, today, with my own hands.

hunks.baseline: I broke the neck of the fanatic blocking my way and used his body to block an arrow flying in from ahead.
hunks.sol: I broke the neck of the fanatic blocking my way and used his body to shield myself from an arrow flying in from ahead.

hunks.baseline: The mana-infused arrowhead pierced the corpse, grazed my cheek, then lodged in the eye of a fanatic who happened to be nearby.
hunks.sol: Its mana-infused head punched through the corpse, grazed my cheek, then lodged in the eye of another fanatic nearby.

hunks.baseline: A cry of pain rang out amid the spray of blood.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed as he screamed in pain. Moments later, a cold slicing sound cut the scream short.

hunks.baseline: But the scream faded away as if washed clean, before long.
With a cold slicing sound.
A red line crossed the fanatic’s neck. A heavy voice, announcing his death, rang out.
hunks.sol: A red line appeared across the fanatic’s neck. A deep voice pronounced his death.

hunks.baseline: The body crumpled like a scarecrow and never moved again. Only then did faint beads of blood begin to well along the cut surface of the severed neck.
hunks.sol: His body crumpled like a scarecrow and never moved again. Only then did faint beads of blood begin to gather on the cut surface of his neck.

hunks.baseline: *This is…*
hunks.sol: *That was…*

hunks.baseline: Even I, who had faced countless powerful fighters, couldn’t help being astonished by the skill.
hunks.sol: Even after facing countless powerful fighters, I couldn’t help being astonished by the skill. I stopped and looked at the speaker, eyes wide.

hunks.baseline: I came to a stop and looked at the speaker, eyes wide.
Among the fanatics surrounding us on every side, a sturdy old man stood tall as an iron tower, looking at me.
hunks.sol: Among the fanatics surrounding me stood a sturdy old man, tall as an iron tower, looking straight at me.

hunks.baseline: A turban was wrapped tightly around his head, not a single strand of hair showing. His back was straight, his gaze deep and still.
hunks.sol: His turban was wrapped so carefully that not a strand of hair escaped it. His back was straight, his gaze deep and still.

hunks.baseline: I’d felt it ever since I first opened my eyes in this place: the old man was immensely powerful.
hunks.sol: I’d sensed it from the moment I opened my eyes here: the old man was immensely powerful.

hunks.baseline: Not just as an Awakened one of the kind known in the modern world as a Hunter, but as a martial artist in his own right.
hunks.sol: Not merely as one of the Awakened known as Hunters in the modern world, but as a martial artist in his own right.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I realized instinctively:
If the Doppelganger was the inviolable symbol of divinity, revered by the fanatics, then this old man was the real commander-in-chief—and the core of their fighting force.
hunks.sol: And I knew instinctively that if the Doppelganger was the untouchable symbol the fanatics revered, this old man was their real commander-in-chief and the heart of their fighting force.

hunks.baseline: “Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin… Is that right? That’s one hell of a long name.”
hunks.sol: “Yahya Muhammad Ahmad Bedouin… Did I get that right? That’s one hell of a long name.”

hunks.baseline: As I read aloud the information in the holographic window floating above his head, the old man’s eyes widened in surprise.
hunks.sol: I read the information in the holographic window floating above his head. Surprise filled the old man’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: “God told me, you crazy old bastard.”
hunks.sol: “God told me, you crazy old man.”

hunks.baseline: “Lies. God would never tell something like that to the king of the wicked heretics.”
hunks.sol: “Nonsense. God would never tell such a thing to the king of the wicked heretics.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re the one talking nonsense. I’m an atheist, so I’m not a heretic—and I’m definitely not a king.”
hunks.sol: “You’re the one talking nonsense. I’m an atheist, so I’m not a heretic—and I’m sure as hell not a king.”

hunks.baseline: “Come on, sir. It’s time to take your pills.”
hunks.sol: “Sir, it’s time to take your pills.”

hunks.baseline: His robe slipped from his shoulder and spread over the ground.
hunks.sol: The robe slipped from his shoulders and spread over the ground.

hunks.baseline: The old man held a crooked staff in one hand and a scimitar—in Murim, you might call it a curved saber—in the other. As he stepped forward, the air around us turned cold and the circle closing in around me tightened.
hunks.sol: Holding a crooked staff in one hand and a scimitar—what Murim would call a curved saber—in the other, the old man stepped forward. The air grew cold, and the ring around me tightened.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t just the old man in front of me. I could see more than thirty men in black, wrapped head to toe in black robes and turbans, scattered among the fanatics.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t only the old man. Scattered among the fanatics were thirty or so figures wrapped head to toe in black robes and turbans.

hunks.baseline: Every last one of them was a skilled fighter who could hold their own anywhere in the world.
And unlike Hunters, who weren’t used to killing other people, they showed not a hint of hesitation.
hunks.sol: Every one of them was skilled enough to hold their own anywhere in the world. And unlike Hunters who weren’t used to killing other people, they showed no hesitation at all.

hunks.baseline: It might not have been a mere trick of the eye that made the black-clad men overlap with the martial artists of Dark Heaven in my mind.
hunks.sol: Perhaps it wasn’t my imagination that I saw the martial artists of Dark Heaven superimposed on them.

hunks.baseline: They resembled each other to a disturbing degree.
They were alike in their blind loyalty and faith in one being, and even more so in their willingness to do any terrible thing for that being.
hunks.sol: They were disturbingly alike: blindly loyal to one being, utterly devoted to him, and willing to do any terrible thing in his name.

hunks.baseline: There were too many people in the world who deserved to be killed. That was all.
hunks.sol: There were too many people in the world who needed killing. That was all.

hunks.baseline: Deep down, I had a vague sense that an absolute being called God might exist in this world. But I didn’t believe in him or pledge my loyalty to him.
hunks.sol: Deep down, I vaguely suspected that a supreme being called God existed in this world. But I didn’t believe in him or pledge my loyalty to him.

hunks.baseline: In the end, it was people who achieved things in the face of hardship.
hunks.sol: In the end, people were the ones who accomplished things through hardship. Like countless others, I’d survived that way.

hunks.baseline: I’d survived that way, just like countless others.

But if that god was the one who’d slipped a beat-up capsule to someone who’d suddenly lost his job a year ago—to a young man climbing a steep alley, worried about how he’d get through this month… Well, in that case, I might be willing to believe in him a little.
hunks.sol: But if God was the one who’d slipped a beat-up capsule to someone who’d suddenly lost his job a year ago—to a young man climbing a steep alley, worried about how he’d make it through the month… Well, I might be willing to believe in him a little.

hunks.baseline: “Then your deaths at my hands will be God’s will, too.”
hunks.sol: “Then dying by my hand must be God’s will, too.”

hunks.baseline: With a low mutter, I grabbed at the empty air. In that place where there had been nothing but air and dust, I caught a spear that had been away from my side for a while.
hunks.sol: I muttered the words and closed my hand around empty air. Where there had been nothing but air and dust, my fingers caught a spear that had been away from my side for a while.

hunks.baseline: A stubborn crease formed between the old man’s brows as he witnessed something magic couldn’t explain.
hunks.sol: The old man saw something even magic couldn’t explain, and a stubborn crease formed between his brows.

hunks.baseline: I wanted to tell the old man in front of me, and the fanatics all around us, that the real demon was running away and leaving them behind. That the monster they called a prophet was racing toward a new catastrophe.
hunks.sol: I wanted to tell him, and all the fanatics around us, that the real demon was abandoning them. That the monster they called the Prophet was racing toward a new catastrophe.

hunks.baseline: But instead of answering, I stepped forward. The wind burst and space vanished as I charged.
hunks.sol: Instead, I stepped forward. The wind burst, space vanished, and I charged.

hunks.baseline: A wave of scorching heat swept away the darkness. The White Flame spearhead traced a path no one could block.
hunks.sol: A scorching wind swept away the darkness. White Flame’s spearhead traced a path no one could block.
